title: reading-notes-llm-efficiency-mike-chen
content:
Quick scratchpad / reading summary focused on LLM inference efficiency (latency/cost) - notes to self and things to try for runtime. Mostly rough, will clean and move to Confluence later.

High-level goals:
- Reduce p99 latency for short-chat workloads while keeping cost per token low.
- Improve CPU/GPU utilization for mixed workloads (chat + long-completion).
- Understand tradeoffs across quantization schemes + kernel choices.

Papers / posts skimmed (high level takeaways):
1) Adaptive KV Caching for Low-Latency Decoding (arXiv) - key ideas:
   - Cache recent KV slices aggressively, evict by token importance rather than LRU. For chat workloads with many short-turn messages, this yields big p50/p95 wins.
   - Takeaway: Our prefix cache eviction should consider conversation boundary metadata (system/user) - not just time.
   - TODO: prototype weighted-eviction policy in the local cache simulator and run on reddit-chat sample.

2) Batching Strategies for Real-Time LLMs (SysML/NeurIPS workshop blog) - key ideas:
   - Dynamic batching with max-wait heuristics outperforms fixed-window batching for unpredictable arrival rates.
   - Multi-tenant fairness: strictly FIFO batching causes starvation; use per-customer soft-priority tokens.
   - Takeaway: add max-wait, and implement soft-priority tokens for reserved customers (Dedicated).

3) Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models (ICLR paper + blog) - key ideas:
   - Mixed-precision (8-bit for attention + 4-bit for feedforward) gives good accuracy/cost sweet spot.
   - Calibration budgets matter: cheap calibration datasets can avoid regressions.
   - Takeaway: add a recommended quantization profile to Redwood Optimize that maps workload types -> profile. Need eval harness to detect regressions.

4) Kernel selection for causal attention (open-source runtime blog/GH) - key ideas:
   - Different kernel implementations shine at different sequence lengths. Auto-selecting kernel by predicted sequence length distribution reduces throughput tail.
   - For long prefix + short generation, switching kernels mid-request is helpful but tricky.
   - Takeaway: add sequence-length aware kernel selection and safe fallback path. Log when kernel switches happen.

Conference takeaways / talk notes (NeurIPS 2024 sessions + workshop summaries):
- Many teams emphasize end-to-end measurement: token-level tracing from API -> runtime -> kernel. We should instrument better (more granular traces in Console).
- Benchmarks are moving beyond throughput to include per-conversation cost + p99 latency under mixed traffic. Consider adding a "conversation SLO" metric in Redwood Console.
- There's growing interest in hybrid CPU/GPU decoders for short responses (embedding first-stage on CPU then GPU decode) - saves GPU time for tiny requests. Worth simulation.

Notes / ideas specific to Redwood runtime: 
- KV cache eviction: default LRU feels wrong for chat. Add conversation-aware eviction and a fast path for single-turn requests (no cache lookup) to reduce overhead.
- Batching: implement adaptive max-wait per-customer tier; Dedicated customers get lower max-wait but also higher batch size caps (configurable).
- Quantization: integrate a lightweight offline eval harness in Optimize to run a small set of prompts (critical flows) per quant profile and surface quality regressions in Console.
- Kernel selection: keep a small table mapping (model, seq_len_bucket) -> kernel, populate via nightly microbenchmarks. Expose override in Dedicated config.

Short experiments to run (prio order):
1) Simulated chat workload (mixed short/long) replay using production traces: test weighted-eviction vs LRU for KV cache - measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per token. (Owner: me)
2) Implement max-wait heuristic in local batching sim and test latency vs throughput across arrival patterns (Poisson, bursty). (Owner: Aisha)
3) Run quantization profiles on small eval set (50 prompts) and measure delta for rouge/accuracy for downstream tasks we care about (generation + code). (Owner: Ruth)
4) Nightly kernel microbench that records throughput by seq_len bucket, writes metrics to /metrics/kernel-selection. (Low-effort)

Open questions / risks:
- How much rollout complexity does per-tenant kernel selection introduce? Need canary path for Dedicated only first.
- What is the minimum calibration set that avoids quality regressions across languages? If too big, Optimize onboarding slows down.
- CPU-first hybrid decoding: network roundtrip + CPU scheduling complexity could negate benefits. Must validate end-to-end latency.

Links I want to consolidate in Confluence:
- KV-cache design doc (internal) - CONFLUENCE-1234
- Batching sim + code - GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/432
- Quantization experiments notebook - link will go here after Ruth uploads (JIRA-ENG-2048)

Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight. After the experiments above, summarize results and propose one small, high-confidence change (likely cache eviction tweak or max-wait change) for a canary rollout to Dedicated to measure real customer impact.

Meeting sync items for next infra sync:
- Quick demo of batching sim results (5 min)
- Request a small Dedicated canary cluster for kernel-selection experiments
- Ask SRE about tracing overhead for token-level traces

End.
